claim: Extramedullary erythropoiesis is not expected in healthy adult mice.
source: Extramedullary erythropoiesis is not expected in healthy adult mice, but erythropoietic gene expression was elevated in lineage-depleted spleen cells from Cd47−/− mice.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about normal mouse physiology.

claim: Erythropoietic gene expression was elevated in lineage-depleted spleen cells from Cd47−/− mice.
source: Extramedullary erythropoiesis is not expected in healthy adult mice, but erythropoietic gene expression was elevated in lineage-depleted spleen cells from Cd47−/− mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from bulk RNA sequencing and flow cytometry analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: Expression of several genes associated with early stages of erythropoiesis was elevated in mice lacking CD47.
source: Expression of several genes associated with early stages of erythropoiesis was elevated in mice lacking CD47 or its signaling ligand thrombospondin-1, consistent with previous evidence that this signaling pathway inhibits expression of multipotent stem cell transcription factors in spleen.
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data and flow cytometry presented in the manuscript, and references previous evidence.

claim: Expression of several genes associated with early stages of erythropoiesis was elevated in mice lacking thrombospondin-1.
source: Expression of several genes associated with early stages of erythropoiesis was elevated in mice lacking CD47 or its signaling ligand thrombospondin-1, consistent with previous evidence that this signaling pathway inhibits expression of multipotent stem cell transcription factors in spleen.
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data and flow cytometry presented in the manuscript.

claim: The CD47/thrombospondin-1 signaling pathway inhibits expression of multipotent stem cell transcription factors in spleen.
source: Expression of several genes associated with early stages of erythropoiesis was elevated in mice lacking CD47 or its signaling ligand thrombospondin-1, consistent with previous evidence that this signaling pathway inhibits expression of multipotent stem cell transcription factors in spleen.
evidence: This claim references previous evidence from prior studies.

claim: Cells expressing markers of committed erythroid progenitors were more abundant in Cd47−/− spleens.
source: In contrast, cells expressing markers of committed erythroid progenitors were more abundant in Cd47−/− spleens but significantly depleted in Thbs1−/− spleens.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cells expressing markers of committed erythroid progenitors were significantly depleted in Thbs1−/− spleens.
source: In contrast, cells expressing markers of committed erythroid progenitors were more abundant in Cd47−/− spleens but significantly depleted in Thbs1−/− spleens.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Loss of CD47 is associated with accumulation of Ter119−CD34+ progenitors in spleen.
source: Single-cell transcriptome and flow cytometry analyses indicated that loss of CD47 is associated with accumulation and increased proliferation in spleen of Ter119−CD34+ progenitors and Ter119+CD34− committed erythroid progenitors with elevated mRNA expression of Kit, Ermap, and Tfrc.
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing and flow cytometry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Loss of CD47 is associated with increased proliferation of Ter119−CD34+ progenitors in spleen.
source: Single-cell transcriptome and flow cytometry analyses indicated that loss of CD47 is associated with accumulation and increased proliferation in spleen of Ter119−CD34+ progenitors and Ter119+CD34− committed erythroid progenitors with elevated mRNA expression of Kit, Ermap, and Tfrc.
evidence: This is supported by Ki67 expression data from flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing.

claim: Loss of CD47 is associated with accumulation of Ter119+CD34− committed erythroid progenitors in spleen.
source: Single-cell transcriptome and flow cytometry analyses indicated that loss of CD47 is associated with accumulation and increased proliferation in spleen of Ter119−CD34+ progenitors and Ter119+CD34− committed erythroid progenitors with elevated mRNA expression of Kit, Ermap, and Tfrc.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing data.

claim: Loss of CD47 is associated with increased proliferation of Ter119+CD34− committed erythroid progenitors in spleen.
source: Single-cell transcriptome and flow cytometry analyses indicated that loss of CD47 is associated with accumulation and increased proliferation in spleen of Ter119−CD34+ progenitors and Ter119+CD34− committed erythroid progenitors with elevated mRNA expression of Kit, Ermap, and Tfrc.
evidence: This is supported by Ki67 expression data from flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing.

claim: Ter119−CD34+ and Ter119+CD34− progenitors in Cd47−/− spleens have elevated mRNA expression of Kit.
source: Single-cell transcriptome and flow cytometry analyses indicated that loss of CD47 is associated with accumulation and increased proliferation in spleen of Ter119−CD34+ progenitors and Ter119+CD34− committed erythroid progenitors with elevated mRNA expression of Kit, Ermap, and Tfrc.
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data presented in Table 2.

claim: Ter119−CD34+ and Ter119+CD34− progenitors in Cd47−/− spleens have elevated mRNA expression of Ermap.
source: Single-cell transcriptome and flow cytometry analyses indicated that loss of CD47 is associated with accumulation and increased proliferation in spleen of Ter119−CD34+ progenitors and Ter119+CD34− committed erythroid progenitors with elevated mRNA expression of Kit, Ermap, and Tfrc.
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data presented in Table 2.

claim: Ter119−CD34+ and Ter119+CD34− progenitors in Cd47−/− spleens have elevated mRNA expression of Tfrc.
source: Single-cell transcriptome and flow cytometry analyses indicated that loss of CD47 is associated with accumulation and increased proliferation in spleen of Ter119−CD34+ progenitors and Ter119+CD34− committed erythroid progenitors with elevated mRNA expression of Kit, Ermap, and Tfrc.
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data presented in Table 2.

claim: CD47 functions to limit the phagocytic removal of aged erythrocytes.
source: Induction of committed erythroid precursors is consistent with the known function of CD47 to limit the phagocytic removal of aged erythrocytes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CD47 function referenced in the manuscript.

claim: Loss of thrombospondin-1 delays the turnover of aged red blood cells.
source: Conversely, loss of thrombospondin-1 delays the turnover of aged red blood cells, which may account for the suppression of committed erythroid precursors in Thbs1−/− spleens relative to basal levels in wild-type mice.
evidence: This is supported by previous studies cited in the manuscript (Wang et al., 2020).

claim: Delayed turnover of aged red blood cells may account for the suppression of committed erythroid precursors in Thbs1−/− spleens.
source: Conversely, loss of thrombospondin-1 delays the turnover of aged red blood cells, which may account for the suppression of committed erythroid precursors in Thbs1−/− spleens relative to basal levels in wild-type mice.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the observed data and known biology.

claim: A basal level of extramedullary erythropoiesis occurs in adult mouse spleen that is thrombospondin-1-dependent.
source: In addition to defining a role for CD47 to limit extramedullary erythropoiesis, these studies reveal a thrombospondin-1-dependent basal level of extramedullary erythropoiesis in adult mouse spleen.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing WT, Cd47−/−, and Thbs1−/− mice.

claim: CD47 is a counter-receptor for signal-regulatory protein-α (SIRPα).
source: CD47 is a counter-receptor for signal-regulatory protein-α (SIRPα; Matozaki et al., 2009) and a component of a supramolecular membrane signaling complex for thrombospondin-1 that contains specific integrins, heterotrimeric G proteins, tyrosine kinase receptors, exportin-1, and ubiquilins (Gao et al., 1996; Isenberg et al., 2009; Kaur et al., 2022; Soto-Pantoja et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CD47 is a component of a supramolecular membrane signaling complex for thrombospondin-1.
source: CD47 is a counter-receptor for signal-regulatory protein-α (SIRPα; Matozaki et al., 2009) and a component of a supramolecular membrane signaling complex for thrombospondin-1 that contains specific integrins, heterotrimeric G proteins, tyrosine kinase receptors, exportin-1, and ubiquilins (Gao et al., 1996; Isenberg et al., 2009; Kaur et al., 2022; Soto-Pantoja et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The thrombospondin-1 signaling complex contains specific integrins, heterotrimeric G proteins, tyrosine kinase receptors, exportin-1, and ubiquilins.
source: CD47 is a counter-receptor for signal-regulatory protein-α (SIRPα; Matozaki et al., 2009) and a component of a supramolecular membrane signaling complex for thrombospondin-1 that contains specific integrins, heterotrimeric G proteins, tyrosine kinase receptors, exportin-1, and ubiquilins (Gao et al., 1996; Isenberg et al., 2009; Kaur et al., 2022; Soto-Pantoja et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CD47 binding to SIRPα on macrophages induces inhibitory signaling mediated by cytoplasmic immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibition motifs.
source: CD47 binding to SIRPα on macrophages induces inhibitory signaling mediated by its cytoplasmic immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibition motifs that recruit and activate the tyrosine phosphatases SHP-1 and SHP-2 (Matozaki et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: CD47/SIRPα inhibitory signaling recruits and activates the tyrosine phosphatases SHP-1 and SHP-2.
source: CD47 binding to SIRPα on macrophages induces inhibitory signaling mediated by its cytoplasmic immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibition motifs that recruit and activate the tyrosine phosphatases SHP-1 and SHP-2 (Matozaki et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Loss of CD47/SIRPα inhibitory signaling results in rapid splenic clearance of Cd47−/− mouse red blood cells when transfused into a wild type recipient.
source: Loss of this inhibitory signaling results in rapid splenic clearance of Cd47−/− mouse red blood cells (RBC) when transfused into a wild type (WT) recipient (Oldenborg et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous experimental work.

claim: The species-specificity of CD47/SIRPα binding constitutes a barrier to interspecies blood transfusion.
source: The species-specificity of CD47/SIRPα binding constitutes a barrier to interspecies blood transfusion and hematopoietic reconstitution (Strowig et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The species-specificity of CD47/SIRPα binding constitutes a barrier to interspecies hematopoietic reconstitution.
source: The species-specificity of CD47/SIRPα binding constitutes a barrier to interspecies blood transfusion and hematopoietic reconstitution (Strowig et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: CD47 forms nanoclusters on young RBC with limited binding to thrombospondin-1.
source: CD47 forms nanoclusters on young RBC with limited binding to thrombospondin-1 (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CD47 abundance decreases on aged RBCs.
source: CD47 abundance decreases on aged RBCs, but CD47 on aging RBC forms larger and more dense clusters with increased ability to bind thrombospondin-1.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Wang et al., 2020).

claim: CD47 on aging RBC forms larger and more dense clusters with increased ability to bind thrombospondin-1.
source: CD47 abundance decreases on aged RBCs, but CD47 on aging RBC forms larger and more dense clusters with increased ability to bind thrombospondin-1.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Wang et al., 2020).

claim: CD47 on aging RBC adopts an altered conformation.
source: CD47 on aging RBC also adopts an altered conformation (Burger et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Exposure of aged RBC to thrombospondin-1 increases the size of CD47 clusters via a lipid-raft-dependent mechanism.
source: Exposure of aged RBC to thrombospondin-1 further increases the size of CD47 clusters via a lipid-raft-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Wang et al., 2020).

claim: CD47 cluster formation was limited on Thbs1−/− mouse RBC.
source: Conversely, CD47 cluster formation was limited on Thbs1−/− mouse RBC and associated with significantly increased RBC lifespan (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Limited CD47 cluster formation on Thbs1−/− mouse RBC is associated with significantly increased RBC lifespan.
source: Conversely, CD47 cluster formation was limited on Thbs1−/− mouse RBC and associated with significantly increased RBC lifespan (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Liver and spleen are the main hematopoietic organs during embryonic development.
source: Liver and spleen are the main hematopoietic organs during embryonic development, whereas bone marrow assumes that responsibility after birth (Kim, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Bone marrow assumes hematopoietic responsibility after birth.
source: Liver and spleen are the main hematopoietic organs during embryonic development, whereas bone marrow assumes that responsibility after birth (Kim, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Induction of extramedullary hematopoiesis in adult spleen can compensate for pathological conditions that compromise hematopoiesis in bone marrow.
source: Induction of extramedullary hematopoiesis in adult spleen can compensate for pathological conditions that compromise hematopoiesis in bone marrow (Cenariu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CD47 is highly expressed on proliferating erythroblasts during stress-induced erythropoiesis.
source: CD47 is highly expressed on proliferating erythroblasts during stress-induced erythropoiesis, and antibodies blocking either CD47 or SIRPα inhibited the required transfer of mitochondria from macrophages to developing erythroblasts in erythroblastic islands (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Antibodies blocking CD47 inhibit the transfer of mitochondria from macrophages to developing erythroblasts in erythroblastic islands.
source: CD47 is highly expressed on proliferating erythroblasts during stress-induced erythropoiesis, and antibodies blocking either CD47 or SIRPα inhibited the required transfer of mitochondria from macrophages to developing erythroblasts in erythroblastic islands (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Antibodies blocking SIRPα inhibit the transfer of mitochondria from macrophages to developing erythroblasts in erythroblastic islands.
source: CD47 is highly expressed on proliferating erythroblasts during stress-induced erythropoiesis, and antibodies blocking either CD47 or SIRPα inhibited the required transfer of mitochondria from macrophages to developing erythroblasts in erythroblastic islands (Yang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Treatment with a CD47 antibody enhanced splenomegaly in an anemic stress model.
source: Notably, treatment with a CD47 antibody enhanced splenomegaly in the anemic stress model.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work (Yang et al., 2022).

claim: Cd47−/− mice derived using CRISPR/Cas9 exhibited hemolytic anemia.
source: Consistent with the absence of inhibitory SIRPα signaling that limits clearance of aged RBC (Fossati-Jimack et al., 2002; Lutz and Bogdanova, 2013), Cd47−/− mice derived using CRISPR/Cas9 exhibited hemolytic anemia and splenomegaly (Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Cd47−/− mice derived using CRISPR/Cas9 exhibited splenomegaly.
source: Consistent with the absence of inhibitory SIRPα signaling that limits clearance of aged RBC (Fossati-Jimack et al., 2002; Lutz and Bogdanova, 2013), Cd47−/− mice derived using CRISPR/Cas9 exhibited hemolytic anemia and splenomegaly (Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CD47-dependent thrombospondin-1 signaling regulates the differentiation of multipotent stem cells in a stage-specific manner.
source: Conversely, CD47-dependent thrombospondin-1 signaling regulates the differentiation of multipotent stem cells in a stage-specific manner (Kaur et al., 2013; Nath et al., 2018; Porpiglia et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Thbs1−/− mouse spleens have more abundant Sox2+ stem cells.
source: and both Thbs1−/− and Cd47−/− mouse spleens have more abundant Sox2+ stem cells and higher mRNA expression of the multipotent stem cell transcription factors Myc, Sox2, Oct4, and Klf4 (Kaur et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Cd47−/− mouse spleens have more abundant Sox2+ stem cells.
source: and both Thbs1−/− and Cd47−/− mouse spleens have more abundant Sox2+ stem cells and higher mRNA expression of the multipotent stem cell transcription factors Myc, Sox2, Oct4, and Klf4 (Kaur et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Thbs1−/− mouse spleens have higher mRNA expression of the multipotent stem cell transcription factors Myc, Sox2, Oct4, and Klf4.
source: and both Thbs1−/− and Cd47−/− mouse spleens have more abundant Sox2+ stem cells and higher mRNA expression of the multipotent stem cell transcription factors Myc, Sox2, Oct4, and Klf4 (Kaur et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Cd47−/− mouse spleens have higher mRNA expression of the multipotent stem cell transcription factors Myc, Sox2, Oct4, and Klf4.
source: and both Thbs1−/− and Cd47−/− mouse spleens have more abundant Sox2+ stem cells and higher mRNA expression of the multipotent stem cell transcription factors Myc, Sox2, Oct4, and Klf4 (Kaur et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Spleen enlargement was previously reported in Cd47−/− mice.
source: We confirmed the previously reported spleen enlargement in Cd47−/− mice (Bian et al., 2016; Nath et al., 2018), but we did not observe significant spleen enlargement in Thbs1−/− mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This references previous studies and is confirmed by data in the current manuscript.

claim: The current study confirmed spleen enlargement in Cd47−/− mice.
source: We confirmed the previously reported spleen enlargement in Cd47−/− mice (Bian et al., 2016; Nath et al., 2018), but we did not observe significant spleen enlargement in Thbs1−/− mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by visual evidence in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No significant spleen enlargement was observed in Thbs1−/− mice.
source: We confirmed the previously reported spleen enlargement in Cd47−/− mice (Bian et al., 2016; Nath et al., 2018), but we did not observe significant spleen enlargement in Thbs1−/− mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by visual evidence in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Total spleen cell number was significantly higher in Cd47−/− mice compared to WT mice.
source: The spleen enlargement was associated with a significantly higher total spleen cell number in a single cell suspension after RBC lysis in Cd47−/− mice compared to WT and Thbs1−/− mice (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Total spleen cell number was significantly higher in Cd47−/− mice compared to Thbs1−/− mice.
source: The spleen enlargement was associated with a significantly higher total spleen cell number in a single cell suspension after RBC lysis in Cd47−/− mice compared to WT and Thbs1−/− mice (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The percentage of Ter119+ cells in singlet cells from Cd47−/− spleens was significantly higher than in WT spleens (p=0.0061).
source: The percentages of Ter119+ cells in singlet cells from Cd47−/− spleens was significantly higher than in WT or Thbs1−/− spleens (p=0.0061 and 0.0322 respectively, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B with statistical analysis.

claim: The percentage of Ter119+ cells in singlet cells from Cd47−/− spleens was significantly higher than in Thbs1−/− spleens (p=0.0322).
source: The percentages of Ter119+ cells in singlet cells from Cd47−/− spleens was significantly higher than in WT or Thbs1−/− spleens (p=0.0061 and 0.0322 respectively, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B with statistical analysis.

claim: CD34 was expressed on a significantly higher percentage of Cd47−/− versus WT spleen cells (p=0.0008).
source: CD34 is expressed on multipotent through the CFU-E erythroid progenitors and was expressed a significantly higher percentage on Cd47−/− versus WT or Thbs1−/− cells (p=0.0008 and 0.0001 respectively, Figure 1C), whereas the multipotent progenitor marker Sca1 was expressed in a smaller percentage of Cd47−/− versus WT or Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0001 and 0.0009 respectively, Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1C with statistical analysis.

claim: CD34 was expressed on a significantly higher percentage of Cd47−/− versus Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0001).
source: CD34 is expressed on multipotent through the CFU-E erythroid progenitors and was expressed a significantly higher percentage on Cd47−/− versus WT or Thbs1−/− cells (p=0.0008 and 0.0001 respectively, Figure 1C), whereas the multipotent progenitor marker Sca1 was expressed in a smaller percentage of Cd47−/− versus WT or Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0001 and 0.0009 respectively, Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1C with statistical analysis.

claim: Sca1 was expressed in a smaller percentage of Cd47−/− versus WT spleen cells (p=0.0001).
source: CD34 is expressed on multipotent through the CFU-E erythroid progenitors and was expressed a significantly higher percentage on Cd47−/− versus WT or Thbs1−/− cells (p=0.0008 and 0.0001 respectively, Figure 1C), whereas the multipotent progenitor marker Sca1 was expressed in a smaller percentage of Cd47−/− versus WT or Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0001 and 0.0009 respectively, Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1D with statistical analysis.

claim: Sca1 was expressed in a smaller percentage of Cd47−/− versus Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0009).
source: CD34 is expressed on multipotent through the CFU-E erythroid progenitors and was expressed a significantly higher percentage on Cd47−/− versus WT or Thbs1−/− cells (p=0.0008 and 0.0001 respectively, Figure 1C), whereas the multipotent progenitor marker Sca1 was expressed in a smaller percentage of Cd47−/− versus WT or Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0001 and 0.0009 respectively, Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1D with statistical analysis.

claim: A higher percentage of Cd47−/− cells expressed Ki67 at low levels compared to WT spleen cells (p=0.0024).
source: A higher percentage of Cd47−/− cells expressed the proliferation marker Ki67 at low but not high levels compared to WT or Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0024 and 0.0003 respectively, Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E with statistical analysis.

claim: A higher percentage of Cd47−/− cells expressed Ki67 at low levels compared to Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0003).
source: A higher percentage of Cd47−/− cells expressed the proliferation marker Ki67 at low but not high levels compared to WT or Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0024 and 0.0003 respectively, Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E with statistical analysis.

claim: The percentage of cKit positive cells was higher only in Thbs1−/− spleen cells.
source: c-Kit signaling is crucial for normal hematopoiesis and is expressed in multipotent progenitors through CFU-E (Lennartsson and Rönnstrand, 2012; Swaminathan et al., 2022), but the percentage of cKit positive cells was higher only in Thbs1−/− spleen cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Epor was expressed in significantly more Cd47−/− versus WT spleen cells (p=0.0077).
source: The erythropoietin receptor (Epor), which is expressed in CFU-E through proerythroblasts, was expressed in significantly more Cd47−/− versus WT spleen cells (p=0.0077) but in significantly fewer Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0017 Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1G with statistical analysis.

claim: Epor was expressed in significantly fewer Thbs1−/− versus WT spleen cells (p=0.0017).
source: The erythropoietin receptor (Epor), which is expressed in CFU-E through proerythroblasts, was expressed in significantly more Cd47−/− versus WT spleen cells (p=0.0077) but in significantly fewer Thbs1−/− spleen cells (p=0.0017 Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1G with statistical analysis.

claim: Cells expressing Gypa, Ermap, and Aqp1 showed significant increases in Cd47−/− spleen cells.
source: Cells expressing the major RBC membrane glycoprotein Gypa, which accumulates in erythroblasts, Ermap, and Aqp1 showed similar significant increases in Cd47−/− spleen cells, whereas only Gypa+ and Aqp1+ cells were significantly decreased in Thbs1−/− spleen cells (Figure 1H, I and J).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 1H, I, and J.

claim: Gypa+ and Aqp1+ cells were significantly decreased in Thbs1−/− spleen cells.
source: Cells expressing the major RBC membrane glycoprotein Gypa, which accumulates in erythroblasts, Ermap, and Aqp1 showed similar significant increases in Cd47−/− spleen cells, whereas only Gypa+ and Aqp1+ cells were significantly decreased in Thbs1−/− spleen cells (Figure 1H, I and J).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 1H, I, and J.

claim: Most cells expressing Epor, Ermap, Gypa, and Aqp1 were Ter119+.
source: Consistent with their known induction kinetics, most of the cells expressing these markers were Ter119+, and the alterations in their abundance observed in Cd47−/− and Thbs1−/− spleens were restricted to Ter119+ cells (Figure 1K–R).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 1K-R.

claim: Alterations in abundance of Epor, Ermap, Gypa, and Aqp1 expressing cells in Cd47−/− and Thbs1−/− spleens were restricted to Ter119+ cells.
source: Consistent with their known induction kinetics, most of the cells expressing these markers were Ter119+, and the alterations in their abundance observed in Cd47−/− and Thbs1−/− spleens were restricted to Ter119+ cells (Figure 1K–R).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 1K-R.

claim: Trim10 mRNA was elevated 50-fold in lineage-depleted Cd47−/− spleen cells.
source: Trim10 mRNA, which encodes an erythroid-specific RING finger protein required for terminal erythroid differentiation (Harada et al., 1999), was elevated 50-fold.
evidence: This is supported by bulk RNA sequencing data presented in Table 1.

claim: Higher Mki67 mRNA expression suggested increased proliferation among Lin− Cd47−/− spleen cells.
source: Higher Mki67 mRNA expression suggested increased proliferation among Lin− Cd47−/− spleen cells, which also expressed elevated mRNA levels of the major erythroid transcription factor Gata1 (Gutiérrez et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on RNA sequencing data showing elevated Mki67 expression.

claim: Lin− Cd47−/− spleen cells expressed elevated mRNA levels of Gata1.
source: Higher Mki67 mRNA expression suggested increased proliferation among Lin− Cd47−/− spleen cells, which also expressed elevated mRNA levels of the major erythroid transcription factor Gata1 (Gutiérrez et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by bulk RNA sequencing data presented in Table 1.

claim: Kit mRNA expression was increased in lineage-depleted Cd47−/− spleen cells.
source: Apart from increased Kit mRNA expression, however, mRNA expression of markers for multipotent erythroid progenitors including Anpep (CD13), Cd33, Sca1 and Gata2 was not elevated in the absence of CD47.
evidence: This is supported by bulk RNA sequencing data presented in Table 1.

claim: mRNA expression of multipotent erythroid progenitor markers Anpep, Cd33, Sca1 and Gata2 was not elevated in the absence of CD47.
source: Apart from increased Kit mRNA expression, however, mRNA expression of markers for multipotent erythroid progenitors including Anpep (CD13), Cd33, Sca1 and Gata2 was not elevated in the absence of CD47.
evidence: This is supported by bulk RNA sequencing data presented in Table 1.

claim: Xpo1 mRNA was increased in lineage-depleted Cd47−/− spleen cells.
source: CD47 regulates activities of the nuclear transport protein exportin-1 (Kaur et al., 2022), and Xpo1 mRNA was also increased in Cd47−/− cells (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by bulk RNA sequencing data presented in Table 1.

claim: Exportin-1 is a Gata1 transcriptional target.
source: Exportin-1 is a Gata1 transcriptional target and promotes terminal erythroid differentiation by maintaining Gata1 in the nucleus (Guillem et al., 2020), which suggested a potential mechanism by which loss of CD47 could increase erythropoiesis.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Exportin-1 promotes terminal erythroid differentiation by maintaining Gata1 in the nucleus.
source: Exportin-1 is a Gata1 transcriptional target and promotes terminal erythroid differentiation by maintaining Gata1 in the nucleus (Guillem et al., 2020), which suggested a potential mechanism by which loss of CD47 could increase erythropoiesis.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: A higher percentage of Cd47−/− cells were Ter119+cKit+.
source: A higher percentage of the Cd47−/− cells were Ter119+cKit+.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Ter119−cKit+ cells were elevated in Thbs1−/− spleens.
source: Consistent with Figure 1F and the elevation of multipotent stem cells in Thbs1−/− spleen (Kaur et al., 2013), Ter119−cKit+ cells were elevated in Thbs1−/− spleens.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A and references previous work.

claim: Proliferating cells with low Ki67 expression were more abundant in the Ter119+ population of Cd47−/− cells relative to WT and Thbs1−/− cells.
source: Proliferating cells with low Ki67 expression were more abundant in the Ter119+ and Ter119− populations of Cd47−/− cells relative to WT and Thbs1−/− cells, suggesting that loss of Cd47 but not Thbs1 increases the proliferation of committed erythroid precursors (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 2C and D.

claim: Proliferating cells with low Ki67 expression were more abundant in the Ter119− population of Cd47−/− cells relative to WT and Thbs1−/− cells.
source: Proliferating cells with low Ki67 expression were more abundant in the Ter119+ and Ter119− populations of Cd47−/− cells relative to WT and Thbs1−/− cells, suggesting that loss of Cd47 but not Thbs1 increases the proliferation of committed erythroid precursors (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 2C and D.

claim: Loss of Cd47 but not Thbs1 increases the proliferation of committed erythroid precursors.
source: Proliferating cells with low Ki67 expression were more abundant in the Ter119+ and Ter119− populations of Cd47−/− cells relative to WT and Thbs1−/− cells, suggesting that loss of Cd47 but not Thbs1 increases the proliferation of committed erythroid precursors (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is an inference based on Ki67 expression data from flow cytometry.

claim: More CD34+ cells are Ter119− than Ter119+ in spleen.
source: Although Figure 1 demonstrated increased numbers of Ter119+ and CD34+ cells in Cd47−/− spleens, further analysis revealed that more CD34+ cells are Ter119− than Ter119+ (Figure 2E and G, left panels).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 2E and G.

claim: Loss of CD47 upregulates early Ter119−CD34+ progenitors.
source: Therefore, loss of CD47 upregulates both early Ter119−CD34+ progenitors and more mature Ter119+ progenitors, most of which have lost CD34 expression (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 2E-G.

claim: Loss of CD47 upregulates more mature Ter119+ progenitors, most of which have lost CD34 expression.
